F2_reference_measure_ambiguity.finding: The corpus states L is 'a linear operator on L^2(V,mu)' (USR-007, OP-CMP-001) and gives the Hilbert-space construction 'H=closure(span{phi_n})=L^2(V,mu)' with inner product <phi_m,phi_n>=sum_i phi_m(i)phi_n(i)mu(i) (DER-QR-001, CERTIFIED) -- but mu is never explicitly pinned to counting measure (mu(i)=1) or degree measure (mu(i)=d_i) anywhere in the corpus.
F2_reference_measure_ambiguity.resolution: Every certified, actually-used instance of this construction (the eigendecomposition of L via DER-SPC-003, the heat kernel via DER-SPC-004, and this project's own independently-verified ARBS spectral reconstruction) computes L's eigenvectors as orthonormal under the STANDARD (counting-measure) inner product -- consistent only with mu=counting measure for the spectral branch. No certified entry anywhere redoes this Hilbert-space/eigendecomposition construction with mu=degree measure.
F2_reference_measure_ambiguity.consequence: The RF-001..005 / BRIDGE B-004 convergence machinery, inheriting 'L' and its Hilbert space from this same branch, is built on L^2(V, counting measure) -- NOT on L^2(V,d) (degree-weighted), the space in which Q=-D^{-1}L and its adjoint -LD^{-1} are naturally self-adjoint (via similarity to L_norm=D^{-1/2}LD^{-1/2}, proven in C-004D).

F3_no_connection_to_the_FP_equation.finding: The continuum object L*P=-div(P grad log P_ss) (row 2116, 'Fokker-Planck Dynamics') is stated as a bare PDE by analogy with standard non-equilibrium statistical mechanics. It is NEVER referenced alongside R_n, G_n->M, Mosco convergence, Gromov-Hausdorff, Delta_M, or any other refinement/limit apparatus anywhere in the corpus. Delta_M=lim L_n (row 2027) and BRIDGE B-004 target g_mu_nu (a METRIC recovery), a different object from P_ss or the FP equation (a PROBABILITY-evolution recovery) entirely.
F3_no_connection_to_the_FP_equation.consequence: There is no attempted derivation, sketch, or even an informal claim anywhere in the ~450-sheet corpus that the continuum FP equation is, or should be, a limit of any discrete graph sequence under the project's refinement functor R.

general_theorem_promoted_to_canonical.statement: For any connected, unweighted, undirected graph G=(V,E) with Laplacian L=D-A: (1) ker(L)=span{1} (standard), so the symmetric generator -L has UNIFORM stationary measure. (2) A reversible continuous-time Markov generator L*_therm with stationary measure P_ss proportional to d must satisfy L*_therm*d=0, i.e. d in ker(L*_therm). (3) Since d is in ker(L) if and only if G is regular (verified: L*d=0 exactly for regular G0; ||L*d|| grows with irregularity for G1-G4: 4.90, 25.77, 145.41, 822.50 respectively), ker(L) != span{d} for any irregular G. (4) Therefore -L != c*L*_therm for any scalar c, for any irregular connected graph: THE SPECTRAL AND THERMODYNAMIC GENERATORS ARE STRUCTURALLY DISTINCT OPERATORS whenever the graph is irregular. (5) The unique reconciling operator, given only the graph's edges and the detailed-balance condition w.r.t. P_ss proportional to d, is L*_therm=-LD^{-1} (derived in C-004D), similar to L_norm=D^{-1/2}LD^{-1/2}.
